So for some countries, nuclear can be part of their long-term energy system, but the first investment that most of the countries, especially in the developing world, need to make is creating the enabling environment, and this is where the World Bank Group can play a decisive role. So we're helping already countries to assess whether the nuclear energy option fits within their broader energy and development strategy and strengthen the foundation that will enable responsible nuclear investments. That means that we need robust legal and regulatory frameworks, independent regulators for nuclear energy and for safe operation, preparing the right human capital and skills, prepare for emergencies and effective security and safety arrangements, how to manage long-term waste and how to sustain public confidence. So when these conditions are in place, and we understand that work and investment needs to go for these conditions to come in place, we will work on financial engagement, drawing on the full One World Bank Group toolkit. This is a good time to be looking at this option. And this is what moving from commitment to delivery looks like. We expect that hopefully we will approve our first nuclear investment for a long time within the next 12 months or so, and this will open up additional efforts and investments throughout the world.
